reference.title: Phrasal verbs
reference.text: Wake up, get up, go out, give up, etc. are common phrasal verbs (verbs with a preposition or adverb). Sometimes the meaning of the two separate words can help you guess the meaning, e.g. go out. Sometimes it does not help you, e.g. give up.

reference.title: Three types of phrasal verbs
rows: What time do you get up? I don’t usually go out during the week.
noun: before or after the particle; pronoun: always between
Put on your coat. Put your coat on. Put it on!
I’m looking for my glasses. I’m still looking for them.

reference.text: A phrasal verb = verb + particle (preposition or adverb), e.g. get up, go out, turn on, look for. When the object is a pronoun (me, it, him, them…) it always goes between the verb and the particle: Here’s your coat. Put it on.

reference.wrong: Here’s your coat. Put on it.
reference.right: Here’s your coat. Put it on.
reference.why: With separable phrasal verbs, a pronoun goes between the verb and the particle.
look for is inseparable – verb and particle stay together.

reference.title: Linking
reference.text: When a word ends in a consonant sound and the next word starts with a vowel sound, we link them and say them together, like one word: turn it off /tɜːnɪtɒf/, pick it up, look after it, take it off.

reference.title: Talking about your morning
reference.text: What time do you wake up / get up? – I usually wake up at… My alarm goes off at… I get up straight away. / I stay in bed for a bit. I feel awful / quite sleepy / awake and energetic.

reference.title: Morning person or evening person?
reference.text: I’m a morning person – I get up early and I’m full of energy. I’m an evening person – I go to bed late and find it hard to get up.

tasks.instruction: Talk about your mornings with a partner
tasks.note: SB 1a + 1d → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You talk about getting up in the morning. Ask these questions one at a time and react naturally: What time do you wake up during the week? Do you use an alarm to wake up? If not, what makes you wake up? Do you get up immediately after you wake up? When you first get up, do you feel awful, quite sleepy, or awake and energetic? In general, are you a morning or an evening person? Would you like to work the hours of a baker who gets up at 2.35 a.m., or a radio presenter who gets up at 4.45 a.m.? Why (not)? Do you know people who get up very early for work? When the student asks you, answer too: your alarm goes off at 7.00, you stay in bed for ten minutes, you feel awful until you have coffee, you are an evening person. If the student makes a mistake with a phrasal verb, repeat the phrase correctly in your answer.

tasks.instruction: Read about Ella’s day and answer the questions with short notes
tasks.note: SB 1b–c + Communication Early birds A p.105 (текст Эллы — в context, фото — image). MODEL
tasks.context:
The alarm goes off at 2.35 a.m. I use my phone, and my partner also sets the alarm on his phone, because I don’t feel very secure if I just have one alarm. I get up straight away. I usually feel terrible! It’s always really hard to get out of bed. Luckily I don’t have to think about clothes, because I always wear a white chef’s jacket and a pair of jeans.

I don’t have breakfast – I just get dressed and go straight to work. I live very near the shop, so I walk to work – it only takes five minutes. I start baking at 3.00 a.m. I’m always desperate for a cup of tea, and as soon as I have time I make one. I can’t really function without a cup of tea. I make all the bread and cakes between 3.00 and 8.30 – that’s when I open the shop.

I usually finish work at about 3.00 in the afternoon, so I’m often at work for about 12 hours. I go to bed at 8.30. Because we go to bed so early, during the week we don’t go out at all. I sometimes go out on a Saturday evening, but I feel exhausted the next day.

Would I like to change my working hours? Yes. I love my job, and I don’t mind getting up early, but I would like to sleep more.

straight away = immediately; baking = making bread and cakes

tasks.instruction: Read about Peter’s day and answer the questions with short notes
tasks.note: SB 1b–c + Communication Early birds B p.111 (текст Питера — в context, фото — image). MODEL
tasks.context:
The Peter Gordon Breakfast Show starts at exactly 6.00, so I need to be at work at 5.30 a.m. on weekday mornings. I’m lucky because I live very near the studio – it’s only three to four minutes by car – so I get up at about 4.45. I wake up on time because I have an alarm that repeats, and I wear a Fitbit which vibrates as well. When that goes off I know that I really have to get up!

For the first few minutes I feel a bit sleepy, but then I wake up quickly. I choose my clothes the night before, and that way everything’s ready. I have a cup of tea, and then I leave the house at about 5.15. I have breakfast during the radio show, while I’m playing music – perhaps a smoothie and some cereal. I’m a director of the radio station, so after my show I usually work in the office until late afternoon – it’s a long working day!

I go to bed quite late, usually at about 11.00. I find it very difficult to go to bed early, it’s always been a problem for me. So I only get about five or six hours’ sleep – but that’s enough for me. Because I get up early, I try not to go out with friends during the week. I only go to necessary events, like work events. Weekends are different!

I know I get up really early, but I don’t want to change my hours because I really love my breakfast show, and I never want to give it up.

Fitbit = an electronic bracelet that measures your physical activity; smoothie = a drink made with fruit or fruit juice mixed with milk

tasks.instruction: Phrasal verb questionnaire. Interview your partner
tasks.note: SB 3e + 5 (Phrasal verb questionnaire) → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). Interview the student with this phrasal verb questionnaire, one question at a time, and ask for more details: Do you ever get up very late or very early? Why? When? What’s the first thing you turn on after you wake up in the morning? Have you ever forgotten to turn your phone off in a concert or the cinema? Do you throw away old clothes or do you give them to other people? Do you enjoy trying on clothes when you go shopping? When you go shopping, do you usually write down what you have to buy? What kind of shops do you enjoy looking round? Do you often go away at the weekend? Where to? Do you enjoy looking after small children? Have you ever asked your neighbours to turn the TV or the music down? How do you usually get around your town during the day and late at night? Finally ask: Do you think getting up very early is a good idea? If you got up an hour earlier, what would you do with your extra hour? Answer the student’s questions too: you turn on the coffee machine first, you give old clothes to a charity shop, you hate trying on clothes.
exercises.goal: Answer the questionnaire using phrasal verbs.
exercises.opener: OK, first question: do you ever get up very late or very early? Why?
criteria: answers at least six questions with extra details
uses the phrasal verbs from the questions correctly
puts pronouns between verb and particle (turn it off, throw them away)
says what they would do with an extra hour
